content.text: This file is already quite polished (progressive enhancement, reduced-motion handling, multi-tab sync, contrast media queries). I couldn't open a browser here (no approval surface for `open`), so I focused on a genuine correctness gap I found in the code: the speed control is arrow-key/Home/End driven (a slider interaction) but is exposed to assistive tech as a plain `button`, so screen reader users get no indication of the current value or range. I'll fix that with proper ARIA slider semantics.

content.text:
Made the speed control expose correct semantics to assistive tech:

- `circleBtn` now has `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin/max/now/valuetext`, since it's actually operated like a slider (arrow keys, Home/End cycle through 3 discrete speeds) rather than a simple button.
- `updateLabels()` keeps `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext` in sync with the current speed and pause state.
- Removed the redundant `aria-live="polite"` on the visible speed text — screen readers already announce slider value changes automatically, so keeping both would double-announce every change.
- Dropped the leftover post-init `aria-label` override that was fighting with the new label.

I wasn't able to open a browser to visually verify (the `open` command required approval I don't have in this session) — worth a quick manual check with a screen reader/keyboard if you want to confirm the announcements sound right.
